newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-US data take back seat to Fed Sept 23 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-US data take back seat to Fed Sept 23 wk.

text.p: With all eyes glued on Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy meeting, next week's scheduled economic data will take a back seat, according to U.S. economists in a Reuters poll on Friday.
"All of (next week's economic data) will be irrelevant after the Fed decides to tighten or not," said Dan Seto, senior economist at Nikko Securities Co International Inc.
But next week's report on durable goods orders, although considered volatile, may raise a few eyebrows, according to several economists.

John Park, economist at Sanwa Securities USA Co, said he is particularly interested in the sub-components of durable goods. "I'm interested in non-defense, excluding aircraft, because that's your business-to-business investment proxy," said Park.
Consistently slow durables orders would reflect a slowdown in investment spending and could herald slower economic growth. But recent reports have been quite strong.
"We've had two really solid months there, and if we get a third solid month, that tells me that the manufacturing expansion is more broad-based," Park added.
The Commerce Department reported July durable goods orders increased 1.7 percent, and economists forecast the August number decreased by a modest 0.1 percent.

In addition to the durables report scheduled for release next Thursday at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, other key data next week include August existing home sales, September consumer confidence and the final revision of second-quarter Gross Domestic Product.
The Fed will meet on September 24 to decide the fate of short-term interest rates. In a Reuters poll on Thursday, 17 of 30 experts said they expect the Fed to tighten credit.
